sentences.text: Plicatodus was a prehistoric cartilaginous fish belonging to the family Xenacanthidae.
Most fossils consist of scattered teeth, but one rare specimen preserves the head, dorsal spine, and pectoral girdle.
Oliver Hampe formally described this genus in 1995.
The type locality for the genus is the Saar-Nahe basin.
These animals lived in Europe during the late Carboniferous and Early Permian periods.
The type species P. jordani comes from Permian-aged material found in the upper Odernheim Formation.
The Odernheim Formation contains molasse deposits ranging from the late Carboniferous to the early Permian periods.
The species P. plicatus was originally described by Karl von Fritsch in 1879 as a member of the genus Orthacanthus.
Fossils of P. plicatus come from the Kasimovian-aged Slany Formation in the Rakovnik Basin of Bohemia.
It is debated whether P. sp. found in Lower Austria represents a third undescribed species or belongs to P. jordani or P. plicatus.
